draft.title: NREM and REM sleep
card: Non-rapid eye movement sleep has stages that get deeper. Brain waves slow down as sleep deepens, and the body is hard to wake in the deepest stage.
Rapid eye movement sleep has fast brain waves that look much like waking brain waves. The eyes dart under the lids.
In REM sleep the muscles have very little tone, so the body is close to paralysed. Dreams in REM sleep are usually vivid.
A sleeper moves between NREM and REM stages through the night. The two kinds of sleep differ in brain waves, eye movement and muscle tone.
draft.remember: NREM: slower waves as sleep deepens. REM: fast waves, darting eyes and little muscle tone.

a.q: Which pattern of brain waves and muscle tone fits REM sleep?
opts: Fast brain waves and very little muscle tone
Slow brain waves and very little muscle tone
Fast brain waves and strong muscle tone
Slow brain waves and strong muscle tone
a.why: REM sleep has fast brain waves, like waking, and very little muscle tone. Slow brain waves belong to deeper NREM sleep, so options with slow waves are wrong.
a.clue: REM brain waves look much like waking ones.

b.q: A sleep lab records Sam's brain waves becoming slower and larger as the night begins, and his eyes stay still. Which stage is Sam most likely in?
opts: A deeper stage of NREM sleep
REM sleep, because the brain is less active
Waking, because the eyes are still
REM sleep, because the brain waves are slow
b.why: Brain waves slow as NREM sleep deepens, and the eyes do not dart. REM sleep has fast brain waves and rapid eye movements, so slow waves do not fit it.
b.clue: Which kind of sleep has slower waves and still eyes?

a.best: Fast brain waves and very little muscle tone

b.best: A deeper stage of NREM sleep

problems.detail: The right option is the only one without a 'because' reason and the only one that does not name REM or waking, so it stands out in form from the three wrong options.
The stem says the brain waves become 'larger', but the card teaches only that NREM waves get slower, not that they get bigger. This is minor, since slower waves are enough to answer.
